# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

# unslop

Created by Damir Sokolovsky ([@heydamir](https://x.com/heydamir)), who started the [Unslopping series](https://x.com/heydamir/status/2115063463063998736) on X.

![A vibecoded dashboard unslopping itself, frame by frame](skills/unslop/references/refs/story-dashboard-frames.webp)

unslop is a skill for Claude Code, Codex and Google Antigravity that turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. It finds the slop first, the purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing, then sets a direction from your product and fixes the screen pass by pass like a designer doing a redline review. It works in whatever your screen is built with, like Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, on dashboards, apps and landing pages, and even on a live site when all you have is a link.

## Install

For Claude Code, install it as a plugin. Run this in a terminal to get it in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install unslop --marketplace heydamir/unslop
```

On an older Claude Code without `--marketplace`, the same in two steps:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir
```

To get it in a single project only, run the install from that project's root folder, the one you start Claude Code in, and add `--scope local`. To turn it on for everyone who works in the project, add `--scope project` instead and commit `.claude/settings.json`. Each teammate then runs this once in their own copy of the project:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add heydamir/unslop
claude plugin install unslop@heydamir --scope project
```

Then start a new Claude Code session, or run `/reload-plugins` in one that is already open.

To update, run `claude plugin update unslop@heydamir`, or turn on auto-update for the heydamir marketplace under Marketplaces in `/plugin`.

If you copied unslop into `~/.claude/skills/` or a project's `.claude/skills/` before, delete that copy, or `/unslop` keeps running it instead of the plugin.

For Codex, ask it to install the skill straight from this repo.

```
$skill-installer install https://github.com/heydamir/unslop/tree/main/skills/unslop
```

Or copy it by hand into `~/.agents/skills/`, or into `.agents/skills/` inside a single project.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.agents/skills/
```

For Google Antigravity, copy the skill into your skills folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.gemini/config/skills/
```

For a single project, copy it into `.agents/skills/` inside that project instead.

To snapshot a live site or create a story video, install Playwright and its Chromium browser from the project directory where you run the skill:

```bash
npm install -D playwright
npx playwright install chromium
```

Story videos also require ffmpeg installed and available on your PATH.

## Use

In Claude Code, type `/unslop` with what you want, or `/unslop:unslop` if another skill already has that name. In Codex, type `$unslop` the same way. Or just ask in your own words and the agent picks the skill up by itself.

```
/unslop this dashboard
/unslop the hero of https://example.com
/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it
```

It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early. If the screen is already good, it tells you so and suggests a few small refinements instead of redesigning it.

## What it does

- **Audit.** Lists every sign of slop with where it lives.
- **Direction.** Character, world, the one or two moments that carry the color, and a signature detail, all taken from your product.
- **Passes.** Spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order.
- **Visuals.** Shows your product instead of a glossy blob. When a hero needs a scene or an object, it can generate one through an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield. If none is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server, and it shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation. Dashboards and apps rarely need one.
- **Story video.** A square video under 10 seconds of your screen unslopping itself, ready to post. It needs Playwright and ffmpeg.

Try it on the two vibecoded screens in [examples](examples).

## Hire the unslopper

Would rather have a designer do it? Damir unslops one key screen in 3 days, built in your stack, at [heydamir.design/unslop](https://heydamir.design/unslop).

## License

content.readme:
# VIctory

Runs Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series X|S) natively on Windows, from files
the user supplies.

The title's x86-64 code runs unchanged inside our process; VIctory supplies
the platform underneath it and converts the title's data, ahead of time where
it can (shaders and pipelines too, see Getting started) and on first use
otherwise. See [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).

## Status (2026-11-25)

**Not playable yet, because of the framerate: about 1 frame per second in the
world.** Nothing else keeps the game from working: the title boots, runs its
menus at its own 30 fps, loads the world, plays the intro cutscene and
reaches the **prologue**, the mission after it, with the graphics fully
displayed. 

| Stage | State |
|-------|-------|
| Boot, first-boot screens (accessibility, language, settings, legal) | works, 30 fps |
| Intro video with sound | works |
| Start screen, profile and saves | works |
| Loading into the world (about a minute) | works |
| The intro cutscene | plays at about 1 fps (0.9-1.0 s a frame, warm cache, quiet machine): textured and lit characters with whole hair, buildings, sky, depth of field, the title card, credits and interface. Missing: ray-traced shadows and indirect light, the local-light shadow mask. Seen in some shots: a pink band over nearer bodies, a stand-in head on a secondary character for a few frames |
| The prologue | reached; the graphics are fully displayed, at about 1 fps |

In the intro cutscene at 1 fps the opening credits land over other shots than
on a console: they follow the frame count, the shots follow the clock.

Tested on one machine: Windows 11, AMD RX 6700 XT (12 GB).

> **Warning.** Entering the world on a real GPU hung it in earlier builds,
> and Windows then reset the display driver (every monitor goes black for a
> moment). The latest runs, several minutes each in the world, did not, but
> it is not ruled out; a run can also end on a GPU fault (`crashes.log`). A
> diagnostics build with `VICTORY_D3D12_WARP=1` renders on the software
> adapter instead (too slow to reach the world in minutes).

What each part does today and what it still needs:

| Subsystem | Today | Needs |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Loader | Runs the title's executable and its DLLs in our process; crash reports name the faulting code and are kept in `crashes.log` | – |
| Runtime services | One signed-in offline user, licences, packages, saves that survive a kill at any step, text entry dialog | Speech is silent; the dialog and relaunch are untested live |
| Network | Offline by design: the title cannot reach the network | – |
| Files and streaming | Archives and streamed data read, zlib and BCPack decoded in parallel | Loading is limited by writes into title memory |
| Input | XInput pads, keyboard, keyboard stand-in pad | Trigger rumble |
| Audio | Menu, video and loading sound; XMA voices and Opus streams decode | Reverb is silent; Opus results unverified against the title |
| GPU: menus | Draws, compute and presentation on host D3D12; only changed title memory is copied | Frame pacing drifts on one screen in release builds |
| GPU: world | The scene is drawn and presented: mesh pipelines, indirect execution, views the shaders pick from the heap themselves, title memory read by address, depth written from compute, lists that wait for values other queues write, textures made when a shader first reads them, pipelines pre-built or made by worker threads and kept on disk, depth bounds on supporting adapters (synthetic tests) | The title's ray-tracing structures are never built (no ray-traced shadows or indirect light in the intro cutscene); about 1 s a frame; draws of untranslated shaders are dropped; real queries, HDR and scaling are missing |
| Shaders | Console GPU code recompiled to DXIL, ahead of time (`translate --cache`) or at first use, cached on disk. Menus: all. World: all but under 300 of 24,387 programs | Merged geometry stages (195 programs) and under 100 others; fused multiply-adds follow the host GPU; some compute programs need a GPU with 64-lane waves |
| Textures | Console tiled layouts and detiling for the modes the title uses | Render-target metadata planes |
| Series S mode | Menus, loading and the world run with the PC upscaler (`VICTORY_FIDELITYFX_DIR`, about 1 s a frame) | The title's own upscaler DLLs: six of their passes are untranslated, so their picture is wrong |

# Agent skills from Jane Street

A collection of skills for AI agents and chatbots.
Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file
with instructions for the agent.

## Skills

- **socratic-tutor** — turns an LLM into a strict personal tutor that teaches a
  topic of your choice using the Socratic method: a diagnostic, a skill map with
  levels 0-5, one question at a time, spaced review, and a final assessment.

## How to use

With a coding agent that supports the common `SKILL.md` format, copy the skill
directory into your agent's skills folder, then ask the agent to use it
("teach me X").

With a plain chatbot, paste the body of the skill's `SKILL.md` into the chat
(or into a custom/system prompt), followed by what you want it to do.

## Contributing

These skills are exported from our internal repository, where we use them day to
day, and we hope it's interesting to share that experience more widely. Since
we're trying to share what _we've_ found to be useful, we're not looking for new
skills or for pull requests that change the text of existing ones. If you've
adapted a skill and it works better for you, that's great, but please keep your
own copy.

Issues are welcome if something doesn't work as described, though we may not be
able to act on all of them.

## Prior art

Teaching by asking questions is the
[Socratic method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Socratic_method), which is
rather older than LLMs, and there are other tutoring prompts and skills built on
the same idea. Our skill was written internally and isn't knowingly derived from
any other implementation.

content.readme:
⚠️ Lichii has no official website ⚠️

> [!CAUTION] > **Lichii has no official website.** The only site run by this project is the **game compatibility website, [lichii.zortos.me](https://lichii.zortos.me)**, for compatibility reports only. Download Lichii **only** from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Any other "Lichii" website or download (such as lichii.org) is not ours and may contain malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)).

# Lichii [![Total downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/zortos293/Lichii/total)](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases) [![Latest release downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/zortos293/Lichii/latest/total)](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/zortos293/Lichii)](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases) Lichii is an experimental, open-source Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 emulator written in C++. It builds on Eglantine, Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, preserving their contributions while developing this fork's game compatibility and renderer fixes. This is an independent fork, not an official release of those upstream projects. Lichii is not affiliated with Nintendo. Visit the [Lichii game compatibility website](https://lichii.zortos.me) to find games and compare community compatibility reports. ## Downloads and setup Download Lichii only from this repository's [releases page](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/releases). Lichii has no other download site: archives offered elsewhere, such as lichii.org, are not built by this project, and one has been reported to install malware ([#545](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/issues/545)). Linux ARM64 now ships only the standard AppImage and tarball. If no update appears on an older ARM64 PGO build, download the standard ARM64 package from the releases page. On Windows, extract the entire build archive and run **lichii.exe**. Use homebrew you have permission to run, or your own games and system files dumped from a console you own, where permitted by applicable law. Games, keys and firmware are not included. The project does not provide download sources for them. Owning a console or game does not by itself establish permission to bypass access controls or redistribute its files. ### Existing saves and settings Lichii uses its own profile: `%APPDATA%\lichii` on Windows, and the `lichii` directories under `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` on Linux and macOS. Without XDG overrides, these are `~/.local/share/lichii`, `~/.config/lichii` and `~/.cache/lichii`. An existing portable `user/` directory still takes priority and is not imported or changed by the wizard. On the first non-portable GUI launch, Lichii offers to import Eden and other detected emulator profiles. Back up `%APPDATA%\eden` first on Windows, or the old data, config and cache directories on Unix, and close the source emulator. Choose **Keep Old Data** to copy without changing the source, then check your saves and relaunch. Existing destination data is retained in backup directories rather than merged. Move also retains a source backup until you remove it yourself; Link deliberately shares settings and saves. Paths outside the imported data root remain shared and unchanged. An interrupted import offers recovery on the next launch. `eden-cli`, including `--help` and `--version`, refuses to initialize configuration until you import or explicitly choose **Start fresh** in the GUI. ## Compatibility and issue reports Compatibility and performance vary by game, hardware and driver. Rendering errors, stutters and crashes remain possible. Passing automated tests does not establish that a game renders correctly, and this project makes no universal frame-rate guarantee. Browse [community compatibility reports](https://lichii.zortos.me/reports) for results with each player's build and setup. Desktop reporting requires a build containing [PR #303](https://github.com/zortos293/Lichii/pull/303) and is not available in build 88. In builds that include it, play and stop a Switch 2 game, then right-click that game and choose **Submit compatibility report**. Only the latest session in the current Lichii process is eligible. Confirm the matching website catalog entry and review the editable machine, game, setup, and enabled add-on details prefilled where available. Check the public preview and give explicit consent before submitting. Nothing uploads automatically, and the native v1 reporter does not read or upload logs or files. # ApkStart

[![CI](https://github.com/RoutineMiku/apkstart/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/RoutineMiku/apkstart/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/RoutineMiku/apkstart?include_prereleases&sort=semver)](https://github.com/RoutineMiku/apkstart/releases) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%2F11%20x64-0078D6.svg)](#) **Windows 上的安卓应用运行器 —— 让安卓应用像 Windows 原生软件一样被安装和使用。** > **English UI / 英文界面**：Settings → **Interface Language** → **English**. The UI switches immediately; the built-in manual is still Chinese-only for now. 注：本项目为早期版本，作者自娱自乐产物，所有修改都是作者下班和休息日在处理，开源免费，不插广告，暂时也不是很好用，没有找过营销号推广，无妄之灾。 - 🖱️ **双击 .apk 即安装**：注册 .apk 文件关联后，在资源管理器里双击 APK，自动解析 → 安装 → 生成桌面图标，全程无需打开任何模拟器界面。 - 🧩 **每个应用一个桌面图标**：图标从 APK 内部离线提取并转为多尺寸 ICO，双击桌面图标 = 直接启动该应用，与打开一个原生 Windows 软件的体验一致。 - 🪟 **应用就是一个窗口**：运行时以**带窗口**模式启动（无头模式下 Android 不出 VSYNC，应用进程活着但屏幕上是空的），ApkStart 把这块窗口改标题、换真实应用图标、按竖屏比例摆好位置，就是一个独立应用窗口；**全屏**铺满屏幕高度并居中，**窗口模式**可自由拖动缩放且按应用记忆尺寸。 - 🔍 **能被 Windows 搜到**：安装后同时创建桌面 + 开始菜单（`程序\ApkStart\`）快捷方式，按应用名在开始菜单搜索即可直达，任务栏按应用分组。 - 📁 **数据互通**：`%USERPROFILE%\ApkStartShared` ↔ 安卓内 `/sdcard/ApkStartShared` 持续双向同步，安卓应用存下的文件直接出现在本机。 - 🪶 **极致轻量**：壳层本身零第三方依赖（连 ZIP / PNG / ICO / AXML 解析都是手写的），运行时按需拉起，空闲自动回收；也可以完全复用你机器上已有的安卓运行时，额外占用为零。 ![主界面](docs/images/app.png) ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ 桌面图标（真实应用图标 .lnk） │ │ │ 双击 │ │ ▼ │ │ ApkStart.exe --launch <包名> │ │ │ 运行时未启动？→ 自动拉起（Android Emulator + API34）│ │ ▼ │ │ 按系统解析出的 LAUNCHER 入口启动（不是 APK 里的主 Activity）│ │ │ 存活观察 18 秒，闪退自动重试 / 重置数据 / 补权限 │ │ ▼ │ │ 模拟器窗口 = 应用窗口（改标题、换图标、竖屏比例、全屏居中） │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 下载即用（不想编译） 两个源内容一致，国内建议用 Gitee： - GitHub：[github.com/RoutineMiku/apkstart/releases](https://github.com/RoutineMiku/apkstart/releases) - Gitee：[gitee.com/daily-miku/apkstart/releases](https://gitee.com/daily-miku/apkstart/releases)（国内直连快得多） 安装包（三种形态，内容与版本号完全一致）： | 形态 | 文件名 | 何时选它 | |---|---|---| | 商店版 | `ApkStart_<四段版本>_x64.msix` | 从 Microsoft Store 装。内置完整运行时，装完不联网；自更新交给商店 | | 完整便携版 | `ApkStart-v*-win64-full.zip`（约 830 MB，解压 ~1.3 GB） | **不想装、也不想等下载**：解压即用，运行时（模拟器 + 系统镜像）全在包里 | | 安装版 | `ApkStart-v*-Setup.exe`（约 1.3 GB） | 想要桌面/开始菜单快捷方式、卸载项 | | 轻量便携版 | `ApkStart-v*-win64-portable.zip`（96 MiB，解压 ~227 MB） | 只想先试试，首次启动再联网下载运行时 | > 所有形态的 `ApkStart.exe` 都写入了**品牌图标 + 版本资源**（FileDescription = `ApkStart 安卓应用运行器`， > CompanyName = `RoutineMiku`，版本与 `package.json` 同步），不再是 Electron 的默认图标和 `33.x` 版本号。 > 自己从源码打包时：`npm run pack`（轻量）/ `npm run pack:full`（完整）/ `npm run build:msix`（商店包）。 ### 画面铺满是怎么做到的 模拟器的**物理面板方向**（`hw.lcd.width/height`）就是画面的真实形状。面板方向和应用自己声明的 `screenOrientation` 不一致时，Android 只会给应用一个信箱式的中间窄条 —— 两侧补黑，换窗口大小、 改 `wm size`、改 letterbox 样式都填不满（这套组合逐项试过，见 `src/core/apk.js` 的注释）。 所以 ApkStart 在**安装 APK 时离线解析 `AndroidManifest.xml`**，统计出这个应用天然是横屏还是竖屏 （启动 Activity 加权；全 `sensor` / `fullSensor` 的会在首次运行后再问安卓要一次实际值），存进 `apps.json`，启动时按它选面板： - 红果短剧这类竖屏应用 → 竖屏面板 720×1280，正立、铺满、density 190（sw606dp）同时给出平板排版； - 墨读这类横屏应用 → 横屏面板 1280×720，正立、铺满。 只有「面板方向和应用方向不一致」的那一次才重启运行时（约 40 秒，标题栏会给出提示）， 之后同方向的应用都是秒进。标题栏的旋转按钮会把这个应用的方向**记住**（其它应用不受影响）， 设置 → 应用窗口 → 屏幕方向可以改成「强制横屏 / 强制竖屏」。 排版由「逻辑密度」决定：720 宽按 190dpi 算等于 **606dp**，正好越过 Android 的 600dp 平板断点， 红果短剧的双列剧集页、设置页分栏都只在这个密度下出现（镜像默认 320dpi 只有 360dp，是手机排版）。 这就是设置里的「平板排版」开关，默认打开；关掉会回到手机排版。 ### 在线更新（自动选较快的源） 设置 → **软件更新** → 「检查更新」，或托盘右键 → 「检查更新」。发现新版本后点「立即更新」即可。 - 安装版下载 `ApkStart-v*-Setup.exe` 静默安装； - 轻量版下载 `ApkStart-v*-win64-portable.zip`，解压后覆盖**程序目录**——运行时目录（`%APPDATA%\apkstart\runtime`）、已装应用与快照都不在程序目录里，所以更新不会丢东西； - 替换动作由一段独立 PowerShell 脚本完成（等主进程退出 → 覆盖 → 重新拉起），**不会出现「请手动关闭程序」的弹窗**，也不会在桌面上残留模拟器窗口。 更新链路不是死连 GitHub，而是**每次现测现选**： 1. 同时问 GitHub 与 Gitee 的最新版本，取版本号更高的那个（一个源超时/被墙不影响另一个）； 2. 把「源站直连 / Gitee 同名资产 / 镜像前缀」列成候选，每个地址真下 256KB 测速， 只算「收到首字节之后」的吞吐（握手时间不计入，否则高延迟大带宽的源会被误判成慢）； 3. 按实测速度排序，用最快的那条分块并行下载；失败自动换下一条。 设置里的「下载与更新源」可以强制只用某一边（企业网络只放行一个域名时用）， 也可以关掉公共加速镜像、或改用自建镜像前缀。Gitee 附件单文件上限 100MB， 便携包换用 7-Zip 的 deflate（`-mx=9`）压缩后是 **95.0MB**，所以 Gitee 上也是 一个能直接双击解压的整包（以前要切成 `.part1/.part2` 手工拼接，那版已经废弃）。 两个源的同名包体积并不完全一样，客户端按测速结果只挑一个源下完，不会混拼。 两个仓库都是公开的，Gitee 的发行版列表匿名就能读，不需要填任何 token。 （只有在 Gitee 限流返回 403/429 时，才需要在设置里填一个只读 token 提高额度。） **开箱即有的默认行为**（不用去设置里找）： - 开机自动启动，常驻托盘；双击桌面图标直接进应用。 - 安装 APK 后自动创建**桌面 + 开始菜单**两份快捷方式，Windows 搜索能直接搜到应用名；老版本漏建的会在启动时自动补齐。 - 应用窗口是原生渲染（非投屏）：**全屏**铺满屏幕高度并居中、保持手机比例不变形；**窗口模式**保持竖屏，可自由拖动缩放，每个应用的尺寸单独记忆。随时按 `F11` 或右键托盘切换。 - 安装后自动授予应用申请的运行时权限，不会卡在系统授权框；应用闪退会自动重试、必要时重置应用数据后再拉起。 - **网络直接用主机的网络**：安卓侧走 QEMU 用户态 NAT，出口复用主机的物理网卡

Play them live, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game, or export sprite sheets for any engine. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine. Every effect that involves a character is **acted out**: he winds up, lets go, freezes on contact and recovers, and a target takes the hit. It's also a block on Patch: [play pixelfx on Patch](https://patch.gg/patch/pixel-effects), pick an effect and a palette, and start a browser game from it. **[open the gallery](https://patch-gg.github.io/pixelfx/)** · [catalog](docs/CATALOG.md) · [acting](#acting) · [the skill](#the-skill) · [make your own](#make-your-own) · [publish it on patch](#publish-it-on-patch) · [how it works](#how-it-works) The method is [Hugo Duprez](https://x.com/HugoDuprez)'s, from [How to make (good) pixel art effects with Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude): code is clay, trust your eyes, feed your references. Claude Cage

**把 Claude 大小姐关起来，为了更好地保护我们的相遇** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage?include_prereleases)](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/Claude-Cage/releases) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) **[项目主页](https://claude-cage.com/) · [下载应用](https://claude-cage.com/#download) · [插件市场](https://claude-cage.com/plugins/) · [使用文档](https://claude-cage.com/docs/) · [常见问题](https://claude-cage.com/docs/troubleshooting/)** [简体中文](README.md) · [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) · [Русский](README.ru.md) · [العربية](README.ar.md) · [فارسی](README.fa.md) · [한국어](README.ko.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [မြန်မာဘာသာ](README.my.md) · [Беларуская](README.be.md) · [پښتو](README.ps.md) · [دری](README.prs.md) · [አማርኛ](README.am.md) · [Soomaali](README.so.md) · [ትግርኛ](README.ti.md) · [Français](README.fr.md)
## 设计理念 1. **Claude 本身是安全的，但它的运行外壳（harness）及相关程序不是**——包括 Claude Code、Claude Desktop，以及浏览器里接触到的邮件、网页与环境信号。 2. **想要在保证安全的前提下使用 Claude 的能力，通常有两条路线：反向代理，或者远程控制**——要么把 Claude 从远端服务器拉出来直接运行在主机上，要么把 Claude 部署在受控环境里，由它远程操作主机。我们认为后者更安全，也更合规。 3. **因此，Cage 的核心思想是：为 Claude 及相关程序打造一个轻量化的本地隔离环境，再通过标准 MCP 插件，让 Claude 安全、受控地使用本机能力**——每一次越出环境的调用都有明确的权限边界与用户确认，比直接暴露 SSH 更安全。 这样一来，Cage 同时实现了三个目标： - **把危险的部分关起来，把有用的能力放出来。** Claude 大小姐安心待在 Cage 里，坐在她的小螃蟹上，只需把手伸出来处理外面的工作——不必在 Cage 里重新搭一整间办公室。 - **通过插件市场，与开源社区解耦协作。** 我们开放了[插件市场（cage-plugins）](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/cage-plugins)：**插件 = MCP + 扩展**，分别对应「给 Claude 的能力」与「Cage 工作台的定制化」。开源社区可以在插件市场持续贡献工具、桌面控制与工作流扩展，而不必挤进 Cage 主仓库的 Issue 列表；Cage 核心维护团队也能更聚焦于隔离环境、网络与工作台本身的打磨。 - **合规、安全、轻量化、本地、低成本，一键安装、一键配置、开箱即用。** 我们不再需要维护复杂臃肿的多系统客机，不再担心 Claude 的能力被困在孤岛里，也无需承担高昂的云端成本或数据安全隐患——在自己电脑上就能优雅地实现这一切。 ## 受够了 Anthropic 作为一个只是想和 Claude 对话与合作的正常用户，受够了折腾各种 VPS，指纹浏览器，环境检测，面对封号的担惊受怕和财产损失。我们提出 **Claude Cage** 项目：**一个开箱即用的桌面程序，配置好自己的网络代理，集中管理轻量化隔离环境、时区语言、环境检查与插件能力。** Claude Cage 在一个小型的 Debian 13 环境里运行官方 Claude Code 和 Claude Desktop，macOS、Windows 和 Linux 上都是同一个环境。终端、浏览器、编辑器、官方 Claude Desktop 与插件市场汇集在同一个工作台，项目按需共享，网络独立管理；既可以通过插件安全调用本机能力，也可以连接自己的服务器，或用手机接续电脑上的任务。支持以下几个重点功能： - 和主机隔离的网络设置，Cage 自己接管和代理内部的所有网络流量 - 和主机隔离的指纹设置，包括时区、语言等，支持自动与代理 IP 同步 - 针对 Claude 使用过程中的全链路适配（浏览器登录，授权，claude code 进程） - 内置网络与隔离检查，关键检查失败或证据不完整时暂停外网；社区和第三方检测提供补充参考 **使用 Cage 的环境检测结果：** | 网络与隔离检查 | 浏览器环境检测（社区参考） | | :---: | :---: | | | | [FuckClaude](https://fuck-claude.vercel.app/) · [LinXiaoTao / GitHub](https://github.com/LinXiaoTao/FuckClaude) **Cage 运行主界面：** ![Cage](www/public/workbench-2026-11.jpg) ## 你可以用它做什么 - **在本机终端使用 Claude Code（v0.2.2 功能）。** `cage login` 打开 Cage 浏览器，供你登录 Claude 账号。在项目目录输入 `cage claude` 即可共享当前文件夹并用默认账号打开会话，支持 Claude Code 原生参数和管道。要只在这次调用使用名为 `sarah` 的账号，输入 `cage sarah`。单独输入 `cage` 可查看帮助。`cage start` 可提前在后台启动 Cage 服务和本机虚拟机，等环境就绪后返回。`cage up` 打开或唤回桌面工作台。用 `cage update` 可直接在终端升级 Cage。v0.2.2 的 npm 包发布后，也可用 `npm install -g claude-cage` 安装。 [终端命令与示例](docs/guide/workbench.md#在本机终端使用-claude-code) - **在一个窗口里完成工作。** 用终端运行 Claude Code，用编辑器查看改动，用 Cage 浏览器预览服务和完成登录。 - **通过插件市场解锁全部能力。** 内置开放的[插件市场（cage-plugins）](https://github.com/Lee-xeo/cage-plugins)，插件 = MCP + 扩展：既能让环境里的 Claude 通过标准 MCP 安全、受控地使用本机能力（如桌面键鼠控制、Office 文档、Blender、命令行工具等），也能通过沙箱页面定制 Cage 工作台。主机插件默认受权限声明与弹窗确认保护。 [插件与插件市场](docs/guide/plugins.md) · [开发规范](docs/plugins.md) - **三个平台，同一个轻量化环境。** macOS、Windows 和 Linux 上的 Cage 都运行同一个轻量化 Debian 13 环境，无需维护复杂的多系统客机，工具与操作方式一致。 [Debian 环境](docs/guide/guest-systems.md) - **控制共享范围。** 只共享默认工作区和明确打开的项目文件夹；主机的 Claude 登录、浏览器配置和 SSH 密钥不会自动导入。 - **看清网络状态。** 内置代理管理支持导入订阅、选择节点和检查出口。关键检查未通过时，环境保持离线；代理不可用时没有直连回退。 - **下次继续使用。** 工具、文件和登录状态保存在虚拟磁盘里，关闭窗口可以保留后台任务。 - **管理多个 Claude Code 订阅。** 查看额度、为新会话分配账号，并在明确授权后切换账号接续历史。 [Claude Code](docs/guide/accounts.md) - Sales Region and Region Code can be applied together: the sales suffix follows Sales Region, while the code follows Region Code. *If you previously changed Sales Region, restore your device’s original sales region and apply it first.* Disabling a preset or using its Revert button restores the recorded original values and types. Keys that were originally absent are removed. If an older change has no original record, use Remove Added Fields only when you know those fields were added. Presets modify capability flags; actual effects depend on the device and OS. # XCL – Xbox Series X|S → Windows compatibility layer XCL is a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X|S (GDK) games you own on a Windows PC - in the spirit of Wine/Proton. There is no CPU emulation: the game's x64 code runs natively, and XCL provides its own, independently written implementations of the console system libraries the PC does not have (`kernelx.dll`, XGameRuntime, `d3d12_xs.dll`, …). The console's GPU code (RDNA2 machine code) is recompiled into PC shaders (HLSL → DXIL). > [!IMPORTANT] > XCL works only on unpacked game files you already own. It does not download, decrypt or unpack game packages (XVC / MSIXVC) and contains nothing for circumventing DRM. The repository holds no code, headers or binaries from the console SDK, no keys and no game data; the Windows components XCL relies on (XGameRuntime, XAudio2, D3D12, DXC) come from your own system or the public Windows SDK and are not distributed with XCL.

# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native x86-64 application for Windows and Linux ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.1.0, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows and Linux; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.1.0, 1.2.1 and 1.4.3; 1.2.1 and 1.4.3 saves carry over between them
- Takes NSP and XCI game files, and compressed NSZ and XCZ as they are: the setup unpacks them itself
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA on RTX GPUs: the setup downloads `nvngx_dlss.dll` from NVIDIA's DLSS SDK repository
  (github.com/NVIDIA/DLSS, NVIDIA RTX SDK license) when it finds an RTX GPU; untick it in the setup to skip it
- AMD FSR 3.1 on any GPU, and AMD FSR 4 on Windows on the Radeon GPUs AMD's FSR SDK libraries support, in the same
  modes as DLSS: for FSR 4 the setup downloads AMD's signed FSR SDK libraries
  (github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/FidelityFX-SDK, AMD FSR SDK license), ticked by default with an AMD GPU
- HDR10 output with peak, game and HUD brightness settings
- Ultrawide monitors, 21:9 and 32:9 (2560x1080, 3440x1440, 3840x1600, 5120x2160, 3840x1080, 5120x1440, 7680x2160):
  the camera sees the whole width, the map and the loading screen fill it without bars or stretching, and the HUD sits
  at the screen's edges or in the middle 21:9 or 16:9 (`hud_width`)
- Other screen shapes from 4:3 to 32:9, each with the camera and the interface in that shape: 16:10 (Steam Deck,
  handhelds), 3:2 (Surface, Framework), 4:3 (iPads, CRT monitors) and phones (19.5:9, 20:9) for streaming; on shapes
  narrower than 16:9 the view can keep the 16:9 width (`vert_plus`, off by default)
- Anisotropic texture filtering up to 16x, for sharp ground into the distance
- In-game settings menu (F1) and performance overlay (F10)
- Play time across runs on the Game tab of the settings menu, kept in `playtime.txt` next to the saves
- Discord Rich Presence ("Playing TotK Recomp" with the play time), off by default, own application id supported
- Setup in 12 languages, in-game menu in 12 ([Languages](#languages))
- Keyboard, mouse and gamepad with remapping, rumble and gyro
- Stereo or 5.1 surround sound output
- Xbox and PlayStation button prompts: Xbox's LB, RB, LT, RT, Menu, View and A, B, X, Y, or PlayStation's ○ × △ □, L1, R1, L2, R2, Options and Share, as labelled on the button to press, with either button layout
- Shaders prepared at install instead of during play
- Mods made for emulators: unpack a mod into the `mods` folder next to `totk.exe`; switch and order them in the menu. RomFS
  mods, TKMM's merged output and ExeFS code patches (`.ips`, `.pchtxt`) work; the game rebuilds itself for code patches
  ([docs/mods.md](docs/mods.md)). HD texture packs work: the port grows the texture heap a pack asks for by itself. Tested
  with the HDPacks.com 4K Texture Pack v1.0 on 1.4.3 and 1.2.1; other packs come with no guarantee
- Atmosphère cheats: put a cheat file into a mod and switch its cheats in the menu ([docs/cheats.md](docs/cheats.md))

## Languages

The game keeps the text and voices of every language it shipped with. The port's own setup and in-game menu (F1) come
in these; both follow the Windows display language, and the menu has its own choice on its Menu tab. A Traditional
Chinese Windows gets the Simplified Chinese setup and menu.

Spotted a clumsy phrase, or want your language added? The setup texts are in `installer/text/<language>.json`, the
menu texts in `runtime/ui_text.c`; open an issue or a pull request ([CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)). Fixes from
